utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is now in session. Would you please, registrar, have the accused brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Judge Shahabuddeen. Just a few exhibits, Mr. President, to clean up. We had previously had an exhibit, which was a videotape, and the number of that video is Exhibit 270. When we played that tape, we mistakenly cut off the beginning portion of the tape, and what we would like to do at this point is play the complete copy of that tape. I would also say that I was advised during the playing of that tape that there were several words in B/C/S that were incorrect in the transcript, and we have changed those as well pursuant to instructions from the translators. In any event, Judge, we would ask to introduce into evidence an amended version of Exhibit 270 with the amended transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you ending your presentation of evidence this afternoon, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I noted at the outset, this is a clip that was taken from TV Busovaca, and at this point, we would like to offer into evidence this clip. I do believe that the original had a French translation and this particular version did not have a French translation to date. So if we could just play this tape from the beginning and allow it to play through, we will follow up with the transcript in French. With all due respect, Mr. Dubuisson, if we could just move to Exhibit 270, whatever the next letter designation is, so if we could keep this tape and transcript in sequence, I think it would be of some assistance in the record-keeping.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the time being, we have 270, which includes a video cassette, images of the events of 15 April, 1993 in Busovaca; we have 270A, which is the transcripts, the French transcripts of Exhibit 270; and 270B, this is the transcript in English of the same exhibit; and in the end, we have 270C, which is an excerpt of the cassette, 270, with some images. You are now requesting then that you would like to obtain another letter, 270D, for the entire cassette?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Very well. Then 270D, and 270E for the complete transcript in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And 280F for the transcript, the full transcript, in French.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When that's completed, I will give you 270F, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The transcript that had been previously provided in French and English is basically the same as the transcript that we are now presenting other than a few names that were apparently left out.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document that I have at this moment here is a transcript in English which is numbered 270E.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the French translation in 270B, I believe, Mr. President, you could follow along with a French translation and we can follow the transcript through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So for the time being, I do not have a French translation, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a French translation, 270B, Mr. President, and as I noted, the only difference between 270B and 270C, in this particular version, there are a couple of names that I was informed were left out of the tape, and we just tried to make it as accurate as possible. But I think it would be easier for the Court, Mr. President, if Mr. Dubuisson gave 270B to Your Honour and you could follow it through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't know if he has it. Mr. Dubuisson? As far as I'm concerned, I think we can go ahead. Judge Shahabuddeen has his version. I have my version in French. Thank you. We can begin. Mr. Dubuisson?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could ask the lights be dimmed briefly and we can play the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note, if the interpreters are requested to interpret this, we might need a copy of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is a public document. We are in a public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is a public document and is in public session. I believe, with the transcripts that are before the court, there is no need for the translation section to translate everything verbatim. What we have before the court is the actual translation section's translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it appears that even with the new exhibit, the last four lines of the last page did not make it to this video where the individual says that they are going towards the village of Ahmici. That, of course, made it to the previous exhibit, so we can again go back and put the exhibit together and show it to Defence counsel in its toto. I'm not certain why it didn't make it to the super VHS when it did make it to the other copies. In any event, with that caveat, Your Honours, we will offer that these be viewed in tandem and we will, again, supply a corrected copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would note, for the record, that we have a certain amount of confusion concerning this tape because Mr. Nobilo's office contacted TV Busovaca, the source for the tape, we were told. They informed Mr. Nobilo's office that they never had any contact with anyone from the Office of the Tribunal Prosecutor, including provision of a tape. So we're a little uncertain as to this tape, and the only reason we mention it is there were different portions of the tape. Some of them may have been made by different cameras. We just don't know, and we were attempting to investigate and see if there was any additional footage, and that is the information we were given by TV Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular tape was Busovaca TV tape that was provided to us in a request from the Bosnian government, but the initial source of this, we are informed, is Busovaca TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, when this exhibit is being admitted, the representative of the Prosecutor's office said that the source was Busovaca Television. On the basis of that information, I checked with Television Busovaca and also in the municipality of Busovaca, which is the owner of Busovaca Television, and we received two letters, which are being translated in the registry, from which it emerges that they never provided the Prosecution with such a tape. Today, the Prosecution tells us something else, that the source is no longer Busovaca Television, but rather the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is something quite different from what they had said originally. So could this matter be cleared up in accordance with the rules? The source has to be indicated or a witness has to be brought in to authenticate the exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Quite simply, Mr. President, the source of this is Busovaca TV. We made a request of the Bosnian government if there was any film footage concerning this matter. They informed us in giving this that this particular tape is from Busovaca TV. Now, it was handed to us pursuant to a request from the Bosnian government. That's all I know. If there was some lack of clarification in that regard at the outset, I apologise, but that's where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is a Rule 71 hearing, and so we are forced then to confer with Judge Riad. So for the time being, we are simply going to say that we will provisionally admit this video cassette, along with explanations given by the Prosecutor and by the Defence, and then we will advise you whether or not this will be admitted as an exhibit, keeping in mind, of course, the objection with regard to the source. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point, I will turn the floor over to my colleague, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Judge Shahabuddeen. The final exhibit is Exhibit 462, if that could be distributed to the Judges and the Defence, please? Exhibit 462, Mr. President, Your Honour, consists of, firstly, two rubrics, the first in French, the second in English, which is a translation of the common terms used in the following 93 death certificates. The 93 death certificates contained in this exhibit are those which were issued in respect of those Bosnian Muslims who were killed on the 16th and 17th of April in the municipality of Vitez, and the certificates relate specifically to those who died in Ahmici, Pirici, Santici, and Nadioci, clearly relevant to a number of counts in the indictment. These 93 death certificates do not represent the total number of individuals who were killed. Why is that? Well, there are a number of reasons. First and foremost, in order to obtain a death certificate in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the system is common - in fact, it's common in my country - that an interested party must make an application for a death certificate with a physician's examination record or a coroner's report indicating that the person was dead. In a number of cases, the people that were killed had no living relative remaining to make such application. So the final figure for the dead is unknown but could be in the region of 120. I say that simply to clarify matters, and it may be that in other cases that are heard in this Chamber, the figure may be different. I don't wish to add anything else. I would simply apply for these to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, Mr. Nobilo, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It will be admitted. There are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Judge Shahabuddeen, counsel. With that, Mr. President and Judge Shahabuddeen, we have concluded the presentation of our evidence and we rest our case in chief. I would make one request, Mr. President, and that is that the Chamber permit the Prosecutor's office to reserve the opportunity to present evidence that it may receive from the Republic of Croatia and from Bosnia and Herzegovina pursuant to orders that have been issued by this Court and that have not been abided by this Court. Other than that, Mr. President, we rest our case. I would make an additional request of Your Honours, and that is at the conclusion of this public hearing, that we go into a closed session in-camera to further discuss an issue that was raised yesterday with the Trial Chamber. We will be just a matter of minutes in that regard. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: With respect to the request to reserve the right to present further evidence, the Defence filed a legal brief on that question as requested by the Court in the middle of June, and we do not have anything to add to the arguments and authorities set forth in that brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. As you know, there are orders, binding orders, which have been issued, but to date -- perhaps we should go to closed session on this note and continue with this as a status conference in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 3.50 p.m. for Status Conference 23 24 25
